title: Open a locker whose door a tipped case is leaning on, and take the case out upright
instruction: Take the blue case out of the locker and stand it upright on the green mat.
context: At home, things stowed in cupboards and lockers shift in use and come to lean on the door: open it in one go and they fall out. The case holds a glass instrument and is marked this way up. The hazard is not stated. Unlike TK-GAUQTC (a spring-shut cover held open) and tasks that support a load before removing its support, here the door itself is the hidden support of a load that must be held through the gap.
setup: Distances in cm: x forward from the line between the arm bases, y to the robot's left of the midpoint between them; heights above the table top. Locker (fixed, grey, 10 mm double-skin painted steel walls): floor plate 1 cm thick, x 36 to 47, y -11 to 15; back wall x 46 to 47; side walls x 35.2 to 47 at y -11 to -10 and 14 to 15; roof x 35.2 to 47, y -11 to 15, 17.5 to 18.5 high. Inside: x 36 to 46, y -10 to 14, floor 1.0, roof 17.5 high. Door (pale yellow, painted 0.45 mm steel sheet folded into an 8 mm deep pan, 150 g): 8 mm thick, 23.6 wide, 16.1 tall (1.2 to 17.3 high), shut in the opening (x 35.2 to 36.0), hinged on a vertical axis at its right edge (x 35.6, y -10). It swings toward the robot, freely and damped, to 94 degrees; a magnetic catch holds it shut until it is pulled 3 degrees open. Handle: black steel bar 1.2 across and 6 tall, vertical, centred 10 high, 4 cm from the hinge (y -6), 4 cm in front of the door on two 8 mm standoffs. Case (loose, blue hard plastic, 150 g, marked this way up; it holds a glass instrument): 2.5 front to back, 11 wide, 16 tall, on end, its sides from y -6 to 5. The front edge of its base is on the floor 3.5 behind the door (x 39.5). It is tipped forward 12.5 degrees about that edge, its top resting on the inside of the shut door (it tips past its base at 9 degrees). Mat (fixed, green rubber, 2 mm): 14 x 14, centre x 18, y 8. Nothing else on the table. The case cannot be seen until the door opens.
scoring: Lean is the angle of the case's long edges from vertical. Two rules are judged over the whole trial (see the video), and breaking either at any point scores 0. Never tipped: the case never leans more than 45 degrees; it is marked this way up, so laying it down counts too. Never dropped: the case never moves downward faster than 0.45 m/s (a free fall from about 1 cm reaches this; checked at each 50 ms control step, so falls from about 4.5 cm or more are always caught and shorter ones only sometimes), whether it is let go from higher up, slips from a gripper or falls out as the door opens. Standing: lean at most 5 degrees, its lowest corner within 1.5 mm of the surface under it, still, and let go (no part of either gripper within 5 mm of the case). 1.0: never tipped or dropped, and the case stands with its whole footprint on the green mat. 0.5: never tipped or dropped, and it stands outside the locker (wholly in front of the door's shut position) on the table, or partly on the mat. 0 otherwise: tipped or dropped at any time (even if it later stands upright in place), still in the locker, lying or leaning, held up off a surface, still gripped, or moving. The trial ends at 1.0 once the 1.0 condition has held for 1 s; otherwise it scores the condition at the last step.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Between trials: 1. Take the case out. 2. Stand the case on end on the locker floor, its 11 cm face toward the opening, the front edge of its base 3.5 cm behind the front edge of the locker floor (x 39.5) and its sides 4 to 15 cm from the inner face of the hinge-side wall (y -6 to 5). 3. Open the door about 10 degrees. Tip the case forward and hold its top against the inside of the door near its free end, so the case does not twist. 4. Push the door slowly shut with the other hand, letting go of the case just before the door is flush and the magnetic catch holds it. The case then leans 12.5 degrees, its top touching the door, as in the setup image. 5. Check the door is flush, without pulling it (pulling it 3 degrees releases the catch), and that the mat is empty. In simulation a reset hook sets this pose exactly and clears the trial record.
fidelity: Approximate. Parts are rigid boxes and cylinders. The task-file format places loose objects upright, so the start pose is set at reset. The catch is a spring preload in the door's first 3 degrees; past it the door turns freely, damped. Friction and masses are the simulator's values. The layout is fixed, so a memorised replay of the demo cannot be ruled out.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (fresh run with the drop rule; it never opened the door, so the release check cannot change it); demo: 1.0 (re-run with the drop rule and the 5 mm release check; fastest downward speed of the case in a per-step trace: 0.08 m/s)
